These interact through a Bayesian framework where prior beliefs about kicker quality inform posterior decisions on when to kick. The failure mode occurs when E_k ≤ 0 or when B_c distorts P_{exc} such that S_{max} is underutilized. Dualities emerge between strategic necessity (kick when needed) and tactical inefficiency (overuse of mediocre punters). The system exhibits nonlinearity in its response to marginal improvements in punting skill due to the discrete nature of game states and actions. The epistemic closure requires modeling both the agent’s internal policy and external feedback loops from opponents.
